meta.note: Eligibility rules and deadlines change quietly: verify on the program's own page before applying.

stages.school: Still in school or an undergraduate

routes.name: Operation Outbreak simulations
routes.format: Free classroom outbreak simulations run through a mobile app; a student competition; free lessons, activities, and an open-access textbook
routes.who: High-school and university students and their teachers; no background required.
routes.why: You live through an outbreak from first case to after-action review, in your own school, and see every one of these career tracks at work. The most direct way to find out whether this field is for you.

routes.name: CDC student internships and ORISE research opportunities
routes.org: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
routes.format: Short-term, mostly summer; paid research placements through ORISE run from undergraduate to postdoctoral
routes.who: Current students at any level.
routes.why: CDC's directory of short-term student opportunities is the front door to the agency. A summer inside a public-health program shows you the work before you choose a degree.

routes.name: iGEM competition
routes.format: Team competition, annual, global
routes.who: High-school, undergraduate, and graduate teams building synthetic-biology projects; every team completes safety and security work.
routes.why: The standing student on-ramp into synthetic biology, with more than a decade of engagement with the Biological Weapons Convention community.

routes.name: Biosecurity Fundamentals course
routes.format: Free, remote, about 30 hours, intensive or part-time
routes.who: Anyone; no prior biosecurity background required.
routes.why: Covers the technical and policy efforts to prevent, detect, and respond to catastrophic pandemics, and puts you in a cohort of people asking the same questions.

routes.name: Next Generation Biosecurity: Responding to 21st Century Biorisks
routes.org: University of Bath and Biosecure, on FutureLearn
routes.format: Six weeks at about four hours a week, 100% online on FutureLearn; free to join, with an optional paid upgrade for a certificate
routes.who: Open to anyone, worldwide.
routes.why: About 6,000 people have taken it. One of the widest-reach biosecurity courses available, and a gentle first look at biosecurity, biosafety, and bioethics inside and outside the lab.

routes.name: Oxford Biosecurity Group projects
routes.format: 8-week remote research projects in small teams
routes.who: Students and early-career people who want to test their fit.
routes.why: Designed to help individuals test their fit, grow their network, and upskill in biosecurity, working on a real problem with a project lead.

routes.name: SPAR Biosecurity Track
routes.format: Virtual research mentorship, cohort-based
routes.who: Aspiring researchers paired with mentors.
routes.why: Recent rounds have included a dozen or more biosecurity projects on synthesis screening, pathogen surveillance, and high-containment research.

routes.name: Public Health Associate Program (PHAP)
routes.org: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
routes.format: Two years, full-time, paid; placed in a state, tribal, local, or territorial health department or a nonprofit anywhere in the US
routes.who: US citizens with any bachelor's or higher degree completed in the last two years and a GPA of at least 2.95; you must be willing to relocate.
routes.why: The classic first job in public health. Associates do contact tracing, disease investigations, surveillance, and emergency response, and many move on to graduate school or the [Epidemic Intelligence Service](https://www.cdc.gov/eis/php/about/index.html).

routes.name: Epidemiology Elective Program (EEP)
routes.org: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
routes.format: Six- or eight-week rotation at CDC, another federal site, or a health department, with a three-day orientation in Atlanta
routes.who: US citizens enrolled full-time in a US medical (MD or DO) or veterinary (DVM or VMD) program with at least two years completed.
routes.why: Applied epidemiology for clinicians in training, running since 1975. More than 2,200 students have done it, about one in eight later joined the [Epidemic Intelligence Service](https://www.cdc.gov/eis/php/about/index.html), and most begin public-health careers.

routes.name: CDC/CSTE Applied Epidemiology Fellowship
routes.org: Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists with CDC
routes.format: Two years, paid, in a state or local health department
routes.who: Recent master's and doctoral graduates in epidemiology.
routes.why: Modeled on the [Epidemic Intelligence Service](https://www.cdc.gov/eis/php/about/index.html) but based in state and local agencies, with a mentor and real outbreak work from the first month. The most direct route into a health-department epidemiologist job.

routes.name: ASPPH/CDC Public Health Fellowship Program
routes.org: Association of Schools and Programs of Public Health with CDC
routes.format: One to two years, paid, at CDC and other federal public-health agencies
routes.who: Recent MPH and doctoral graduates from accredited schools and programs of public health.
routes.why: Mentored placements in public-health practice, informatics, and policy. ASPPH has supported more than 2,100 graduates through these fellowships since 1982.

routes.name: Public Health Informatics Fellowship Program (PHIFP)
routes.org: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
routes.format: Two years, paid, at CDC host sites
routes.who: Master's and doctoral graduates with computer science, data science, or public-health backgrounds.
routes.why: Applies information science and technology to public-health problems: the surveillance systems, data pipelines, and dashboards the Data & Technology track is built on.

routes.name: Laboratory Leadership Service (LLS)
routes.org: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
routes.format: Two-year postdoctoral service and learning program, paid
routes.who: US citizens or permanent residents with a doctoral degree in a laboratory discipline such as microbiology, molecular biology, genetics, or bioinformatics.
routes.why: The laboratory twin of the [Epidemic Intelligence Service](https://www.cdc.gov/eis/php/about/index.html): fellows train with experts, deploy on outbreak responses, and build skills in biosafety, quality management, and bioinformatics.

routes.name: APHL-CDC laboratory fellowships
routes.org: Association of Public Health Laboratories with CDC
routes.format: One to two years, paid; tracks in infectious diseases, bioinformatics, biorisk management, food safety, informatics, and quality management
routes.who: Bachelor's through doctoral graduates in microbiology, biology, bioinformatics, or related fields.
routes.why: The main route into public-health laboratory careers, and the one place in this list where a bachelor's degree opens a laboratory fellowship.

routes.name: Public Health Institute/CDC Global Public Health Fellowship
routes.format: One to three years, paid, international placements
routes.who: Recent MPH and doctoral graduates.
routes.why: Program management and epidemiology experience overseas, for people who want the global side of outbreak response.

routes.name: Scoville Peace Fellowship
routes.format: 6 to 9 months, full-time, Washington DC
routes.who: Recent bachelor's or master's graduates.
routes.why: Places fellows with DC security-policy NGOs, including some that work on biosecurity such as the Nuclear Threat Initiative.

routes.name: Emerging Leaders in Biosecurity (ELBI) Fellowship
routes.org: Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security
routes.format: 10 months, part-time, workshops and events
routes.who: Graduate students and professionals; highly competitive.
routes.why: Launched in 2012, with more than 300 alumni across government, national security, industry, science, law, public health, medicine, and journalism. The best-known early-career network in US biosecurity.

routes.name: Epidemic Intelligence Service (EIS)
routes.org: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
routes.format: 2-year post-graduate fellowship in applied epidemiology
routes.who: Doctoral-level scientists, physicians, veterinarians, nurses, and other health professionals.
routes.why: CDC's applied-epidemiology training program since 1951, with more than 4,100 'disease detectives' trained. EIS officers investigate and control outbreaks alongside CDC experts. The classic route into the Public Health & Epidemiology track.

routes.name: Mirzayan Science & Technology Policy Graduate Fellowship
routes.org: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
routes.format: 12 weeks, full-time, Washington DC
routes.who: Current graduate students and graduate degree holders.
routes.why: A short, structured introduction to how science advice reaches government, with a strong alumni network.

routes.name: Horizon Fellowship
routes.format: 6 to 24 months, full-time, US
routes.who: Early- and mid-career people; job placements in the executive branch, Congress, and think tanks.
routes.why: The fellowship behind the [Emerging Tech Policy Careers](https://emergingtechpolicy.org) site, focused on emerging-technology policy including biosecurity.

routes.name: NobleReach Scholars
routes.format: 1 to 2 years, full-time
routes.who: Early-career technologists in AI, biotech, computing, and cybersecurity.
routes.why: Technology-policy placements in government or mission-driven companies for people with technical backgrounds.

routes.name: Fellowship for Ending Bioweapons Programs
routes.format: 12 months, part-time
routes.who: Early-career fellows.
routes.why: Fellows work with CSR's experts to generate ideas for ending the threat of state biological weapons programs.

routes.name: Youth for Biosecurity Fellowship
routes.org: UN Office for Disarmament Affairs, funded by the European Union
routes.format: 3 months, part-time, online workshops plus a Geneva visit; annual since 2019, fellowship since 2023
routes.who: Advanced degree holders under 40 who are citizens of a low- or middle-income Biological Weapons Convention state party; emphasis on young women scientists.
routes.why: The treaty secretariat's own youth program. A past cohort's handbook is now listed in the [Biosecurity Central](https://biosecuritycentral.org) library, proof the pathway produces visible work.

routes.name: AAAS Science and Technology Policy Fellowships
routes.org: American Association for the Advancement of Science
routes.format: 12 months, Washington DC, four tracks
routes.who: Doctoral-level degree holders.
routes.why: Places scientists inside the executive, legislative, or judicial branch, or a nonprofit. A well-worn bridge from the lab into policy.

routes.name: Science Policy Fellowship
routes.format: 1 year, paid
routes.who: PhD or other terminal degree holders.
routes.why: Science-policy experience in biomedical and health research advocacy.

routes.name: Biotechnology Innovation & International Security Fellowship
routes.org: Center for International Security and Cooperation, Stanford University
routes.format: Academic research fellowship
routes.who: Predoctoral and postdoctoral researchers and junior faculty, from the US and abroad.
routes.why: A research home for people working on the security implications of biotechnology.

routes.name: Rosetta Commons Biosecurity Fellowship
routes.format: 12 months, remote
routes.who: People at the intersection of computational biology and biosecurity.
routes.why: Explores how AI-enabled protein design tools can be developed and governed responsibly.

routes.name: ERA and Pivotal research fellowships
routes.org: Existential Risk Alliance (Cambridge) and Pivotal Research (London)
routes.format: Structured research fellowships, mostly UK-based
routes.who: Early-career researchers.
routes.why: Both run programs that include AI × bio and biosecurity projects, with mentorship and a cohort.

routes.name: Field Epidemiology Training Programs (FETP)
routes.org: National ministries and public-health institutes, networked through TEPHINET
routes.format: Three tiers: a three-month part-time frontline course, a nine- to twelve-month intermediate program, and a two-year full-time advanced program
routes.who: Public-health staff working inside a ministry of health or national public-health institute; more than 117 programs serve over 150 countries.
routes.why: The world's largest outbreak-response training system, built on CDC's [Epidemic Intelligence Service](https://www.cdc.gov/eis/php/about/index.html) model. More than 22,000 graduates form the 'boots on the ground' for detecting and responding to outbreaks.

routes.name: Mid-Career Biodefense Bootcamp
routes.format: 2 months, part-time, hybrid: virtual course plus 3 days in Washington DC
routes.who: Mid-career citizens of NATO countries and certain other US allies, typically 10+ years of experience.
routes.why: A fast, structured way for experienced professionals to move into biodefense.

routes.name: Health Policy Fellowship
routes.format: 1 year, full-time executive-branch placement
routes.who: Mid-career professionals.
routes.why: Focused on health and biosecurity policy inside the US government.

routes.name: Biosecurity Game Changers Fellowship
routes.format: 1 year, half-time
routes.who: Mid-career African and US health-security experts with at least 5 years of experience.
routes.why: Placements with leading biosecurity and global-health organizations such as [CEPI](https://cepi.net/), Gavi, IBBIS, and the BWC Implementation Support Unit.

routes.name: Arms Control Negotiation Academy
routes.format: 12 months, part-time, three week-long workshops
routes.who: A competitively selected cohort of rising international-security experts.
routes.why: Negotiation skills for the treaty and diplomacy side of biosecurity.

routes.name: IFBA Professional Certifications and Global Mentorship Program
routes.format: Professional certification; mentor and mentee pairs matched by region and discipline
routes.who: Biosafety and biosecurity practitioners at any career stage.
routes.why: The only internationally recognized certification of competency in biorisk management and related disciplines, with more than 1,400 certifications issued in 89 countries. Check the IFBA page for disciplines, prerequisites, and costs.

routes.name: BWC Advanced Education Course
routes.format: Course on the Biological Weapons Convention
routes.who: People who want to understand the treaty regime in depth.
routes.why: Run by the UN's own disarmament research institute.

routes.name: ACHS Fellowship Programme
routes.org: Asia Centre for Health Security, National University of Singapore
routes.format: Twelve months, part-time, no relocation; one mentored project plus seminars and networking with senior leaders
routes.who: Early- to mid-career professionals aged 25 to 40 who are citizens of, or have worked three years in, an ASEAN+6 country, with a graduate degree or three years of relevant experience.
routes.why: The main early-career biosecurity fellowship in Asia, run from Singapore's Saw Swee Hock School of Public Health. Applications open in the third quarter each year.

routes.name: Presidential Management Fellows Program
routes.format: Two-year paid federal leadership development program with rotations across agencies
routes.who: US graduate students finishing a master's, PhD, or JD by the following August, or graduates within two years of the application opening.
routes.why: The flagship entry route into federal service for people with advanced degrees, including placements at HHS, CDC, and the national-security agencies. Applications open each fall.

routes.name: Museum of Science Public Health Communication Fellowship
routes.format: Six months working alongside established digital communicators to build a public-facing presence
routes.who: Health experts, researchers, clinicians, policy leaders, and evidence-based communicators.
routes.why: A structured way to learn how people actually find, understand, and act on health information online. Built for the Communication track.

routes.name: Takemi Program in International Health
routes.org: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
routes.format: Eleven months in residence at Harvard from August, conducting research and building leadership skills; the program itself does not provide funding
routes.who: Mid-career health professionals and scholars with a graduate degree, publications, and demonstrated leadership potential, from any relevant discipline.
routes.why: A well-known mid-career research year for people from health systems around the world. Applications close December 31.

routes.name: Millennium Fellowship
routes.format: Nine-month hybrid leadership accelerator, September to May, with biweekly virtual sessions, executive coaching, and a ten-day international study tour; participation fees apply, lower for nonprofit and public-sector staff
routes.who: High-impact mid-career professionals aged 25 to 40 from any sector, worldwide.
routes.why: Leadership development inside the think tank that now houses the Bipartisan Commission on Biodefense, for people moving toward senior policy roles.
